articles.title: Robin Williams’ Daughter Calls for Fans Creating AI Videos of the Actor to ‘Have Some Shame’: ‘Leave Him Out of Your Delusional Bulls—’
articles.summary: Zelda Williams is calling for fans to stop circulating AI-generated videos of her late father, Robin Williams, nearly a year after she last took to social media to ask them not to send her augmented content featuring the actor.
body: The iconic comedian, who starred in films including “Jumanji,” “Good Will Hunting,” “Dead Poets Society,” “Hook,” “Mrs. Doubtfire,” and more, died in 2014 at the age of 63. In recent years, his likeness has become a popular target for AI recreation as users continue to create and share augmented videos of the actor.

This isn’t the first time Zelda has voiced her feelings about AI; Back in Oct. 2025, she wrote “Please, just stop sending me AI videos of Dad” on Instagram. “Stop believing I wanna see it or that I’ll understand, I don’t and I won’t. If you’re just trying to troll me, I’ve seen way worse, I’ll restrict and move on. But please, if you’ve got any decency, just stop doing this to him and to me, to everyone even, full stop. It’s dumb, it’s a waste of time and energy, and believe me, it’s NOT what he’d want.”
Just last month, she revived her father’s Instagram account with siblings Zak and Cody in an attempt to “fight back against rampant AI abuse of his voice and likeness on here.”

articles.title: Netflix Partners With British Library, Sets Talks Series With Florence Pugh, Zoe Kazan and More
articles.summary: Netflix has teamed with one of the most famous cultural institutions in the U.K., the British Library, to help “more people discover the books behind some of the world’s most popular films and series,” it says.
body: In addition to the donated collections, Netflix and the British Library will host a programme of events also streamed to libraries across the country about how books are brought to the screen. The programme has already included Q&As with the stars of “Frankenstein,” “The Thursday Murder Club”, and “The Seven Dials Mystery.” On Monday night, Florence Pugh, Zoe Kazan, Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist discussed the making of “East of Eden.”

“Every great adaptation starts with a great story. We are proud to bring these stories to audiences all over the world, but we also know the experience does not have to end when the credits roll,” said Anne Mensah, Vice President of Content, U.K. at Netflix.

“Books and screen adaptations can introduce audiences to different worlds, ideas and voices. Through our partnership with the British Library, we hope to help more people discover the books behind the shows and films they love, while supporting the public libraries that make reading accessible to communities across the country.”

articles.title: Tom Cruise Says AI Is ‘Coming and It’s Going to Happen,’ but ‘People Want to See Real Things’: ‘Keep Creating’
articles.summary: Despite the threat of AI to the film industry, Tom Cruise is confident that people will always “want to see real things” on screen. At an intimate BAFTA “Life in Pictures” conversation in London on Monday night, Cruise looked back on his four-decade career including acclaimed roles in “Top Gun,”…
body: “Here’s the thing: There is nothing like human,” Cruise began, explaining that one of the reasons he is so bullish on keeping the theatrical experience alive is because it brings people together.
“I have nothing against streaming or anything like that,” he continued, saying that seeing a film in theaters is simply “a different art form.”

He pointed to this summer’s box office — which broke all-time industry records by grossing $4.76 billion from May 1 to Labor Day — as an example of the enduring desire for human stories and craftsmanship.
“People want that experience. They’re going to movie theaters,” Cruise said, adding: “I always believe in humanity.”

articles.title: Sense and Sensibility review – Daisy Edgar-Jones leads sober-minded next-gen do-over of Austen romcom
articles.summary: With Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as the Dashwood sisters, this fresh take on a beloved classic is not to be confused with Ang Lee’s. There’s no reason for anyone working on a new adaptation of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility to be intimidated by the celebrated 1995 movie by director Ang…
body: The sisters at the heart of the story, Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, played in 1995 by Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet, are now played by Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles, and frankly don’t look and sound much like the sisters we thought we knew. They look like young women who knew each other reasonably well at uni and are now in a flatshare in London. It is a story of financial and romantic crisis. Mrs Dashwood and her three daughters, having happily occupied a handsome Sussex estate, are forced to move to humble Barton Cottage in Devon when Mrs Dashwood’s stepson John Dashwood inherits their property and effectively evicted them.

Before this can happen, Elinor meets and falls for young Edward Ferrars, a shy and decent young man of a well-to-do family, reticently portrayed by George MacKay. Here, in fact, it should be said that Diana Reid’s script and Georgia Oakley’s direction put into valuably sharper focus something left unstressed in 1995: that Mrs Dashwood (Caitríona Balfe) is pointedly insisting on moving away to the west country rather than endure the indignity of her daughter seeming to be a gold-digger.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban
articles.summary: Major US networks later suspended White House TV coverage of Trump as he headed to New York for a UN summit.
body: CNN, Politico and MS NOW have said they will sue the Trump administration after the three US media outlets were barred from the White House.

President Donald Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
Major US TV networks later suspended their White House pooled coverage of Trump as he headed to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

articles.title: The Seasons review – Portuguese pastoral offers poetic excavation of myth and mapping
articles.summary: The rugged roads and lush vegetation of southern Portugal are showcased in this weaving-together of disparate threads of history and landscape. In a sea of doomsday ecological documentaries, Maureen Fazendeiro’s pastoral marvel is a sight for sore eyes.
body: The abundant use of tracking shots not only takes in the wondrous biodiversity of Alentejo but also facilitates a fluid movement between separate epochs. Observational scenes of green hills, boundless blue skies and roaming livestock are overlaid with narrated excerpts from second world war-era letters written by German archaeologists Georg and Vera Leisner. Credited with producing the first inventory of megalithic monuments in Alentejo, the pair imbues their wartime correspondence with the joy of discovery and the sadness of exile.

Elsewhere, history is preserved in oral tradition. One scene observes a circle of elders, in which a woman laments the rise of fascism and the fall of socialism in song, wistful melodies that reminds us of the years of António de Oliveira Salazar’s dictatorship. Another striking sequence takes a leap of imagination by re-staging a 17th-century myth. In weaving together these disparate threads of narrative, Fazendeiro’s sumptuous film offers an alternative form of geographical mapping, in which a landscape can be read like a text or a poem, to be preserved and passed on to future generations.

articles.title: Death of Cindy Crawford's son Presley Gerber being investigated as suspected overdose
articles.summary: His family asked for privacy during a "very difficult and painful time" following the model's death.
body: Officials are investigating the death of Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, as a suspected overdose, Santa Monica police said on Monday.

The 27-year-old model died at a rehab facility on Sunday, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. The exact cause of death has not been determined, police said, adding there was no indication of foul play.
Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and her husband Rande Gerber, told the BBC's US partner CBS News: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."
Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

articles.title: Heart of the action: why organ couriers are cinema’s new heroes
articles.summary: Whether its a nod to frontline Covid heroes or a return to biology in a world of digital noise, there’s a rich vein of new films featuring organ deliveries, including Runner and the latest Resident Evil. Hollywood loves a ticking clock – especially when there’s a delivery involved.
body: Lately, however, Hollywood seems interested in a different kind of hero – not to mention a different kind of cargo. Forget your nuclear launch codes, stolen diamonds and mysterious briefcases, for human organs are the new MacGuffins du jour, and the medical professionals charged with getting them to the ICU have become unlikely action heroes.

Take Runner, directed by Scott Waugh, which stars Alan “Reacher” Ritchson as a delivery driver caught in a race against time, and Owen Wilson as an organ courier carrying a liver with a life-or-death deadline. “If she doesn’t get this today,” Wilson says of the girl awaiting the transplant, “she’s not going to make it.”

Co-writer Miles Hubley says he and writing partner Tommy White wanted “a device that wasn’t just about money”, adding: “Neither of us had ever seen a movie where the precious cargo everyone wants was a fragile, life-saving piece of tissue.”

Waugh agrees: an organ gives the film “emotional urgency”. “It’s the idea of a protagonist being driven not by revenge or saving the world, but simply by an obligation to deliver something on time,” he says. “You’ve got a deadline and someone whose life depends on you arriving.”

articles.title: David Ellison: Me, Move? I Love L.A.
articles.summary: After insinuations that he was serious about relocating Paramount from its century-old home if the states' lawsuit proceeded, the mogul has now changed tune.
body: Fresh off brushing past California attorney general Rob Bonta with a settlement in which arguably only minor concessions were made, David Ellison is ready to re-commit to the idea of keeping his Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery empire in Los Angeles.

“Now that we reached and announced a settlement, we’re eager to get to work building a stronger Hollywood,” Ellison said in a statement. “Let me be clear: the newly merged company will be headquartered in Los Angeles. We aren’t going anywhere. Our history is here and this is where our future is being built.”

This brings the mogul back in line with his tune circa February of this year, when he was making promises to California politicians about how he would boost local production and bring back glory to Hollywood’s hometown. Then California attorney general Rob Bonta and his posse of 12 states filed a lawsuit in July that seemingly had Paramount on the ropes.
